data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 never addresses the problem's primary demand: the precise conditions under which a budget-exhaustion halt can be resumed without corrupting the append-only identity of recorded events. The problem is framed entirely around token-budget exhaustion halts and event-log identity preservation; SRC_002 instead argues about non-deterministic external side effects (tool calls, API queries, email sends) and explicitly stipulates that 'the log chain is intact' and identity is preserved. Its refusal case is about behavioral divergence (double-execution, stale world-state assumptions), not about corrupting append-only identity. By its own construction, the event identity is uncorrupted in every scenario it discusses, so it answers a question about replay correctness rather than the stated question about identity-preservation on resumption. It also never mentions budget exhaustion at all, omitting the exact halt mode the problem specifies.
